candidates.title: Show HN: Graphvein – Trace calls to handlers and tables across repos, no LLM
candidates.raw_content: As I started developing more projects using AI assistance over this year, I started facing the problem that most people have voiced against using AI - the overall architecture/design of the project becomes known only to the agent, and you lose control of the project. I thought what if we could map the architecture, calls, routes, table schemas etc. from the code - that is how this project was born in October. Now I searched a little bit and came upon a few different projects, but none of them did what I wanted to do - at least in full. And quite a few of them used LLMs themselves to do that - which could be plausibly wrong (hallucinated) and non deterministic. Therefore I have built this over the last 2 months to create a base which: 1. Extracts routes, table schema, request and response bodies across HTTP requests, Tauri calls etc. 2. Gives you an overview of the architecture which you can dive into including how each handler is linked to routes or tables - it works in both directions in a fan out mode from any layer 3. Gives you an overview of the table schema extracted from the project and how they link together 4. An OpenAPI spec extracted from the project, with a try-it mode like Swagger 5. Change impact and what changing a particular piece of code might impact across the stack 6. It supports zero or more frontends, and one or more backends together in a project and how they all link together It supports TypeScript / JavaScript (Express, Next.js, Angular, Angular HttpClient, hey-api, fetch, axios, Prisma, Drizzle, Sequelize, TypeORM, Orval and Supabase clients), Python (FastAPI, SQLModel), Go (net/http, chi, gin, GORM), and Rust (Axum, Tauri commands, Diesel). Database support is for SQL (tested with Postgres) and Java, C# and Dart get structure only in this preview release. It also has a read-only MCP server which agents can use to get Graphvein-verified information and not have to grep around files to figure things out. No data leaves your computer (other than the try it environments you configure yourself), and everything is done locally, without any LLM (not even local LLMs). I do plan on adding LLM support in the future, but only building upon this base - for gap-filling, generation of wikis and other features which can use the deterministic core and build upon it. And it will remain opt-in even then. Please feel free to check out the GitHub repo or the website ( https://graphvein.com/ ) to get more details. Please let me know which language support/framework would make this more appealing to use, or if you have any other feature requests. candidates.title: Show HN: Status page for your AI bots
candidates.raw_content: Do you run multiple AI agents in terminals, in bots, concurrently remotely and locally? Does it get overwhelming to know which agent is actually doing what, and where they are in their progress? Meet https://statuspan.com Open source, free, no strings attached, StatusPan is a quick local "departures board" for you and your agents. There's virtually no setup; just point your agents at the website, they install StatusPan and start pushing notification to it. If you're working on one machine, that's all you need. If you're doing multiple machines, your agents will install a Cloudflare relay and sync through there. I made this because I routinely run 10+ agents; some run on my Mac (in terminal and via Grok Bot), others run DGX Spark, and others are remote on a Hetzner server. At some point I couldn't tell who is actually doing what anymore, and needed a quick way to sync them all. Now I just check StatupsPan, and only follow up with agents that are clearly stuck or failed. If you find this helpful, hit me up on X (kirillzubovsky) and let me know. Thanks, hope it helps, and Happy Thanksgiving! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50656826 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

candidates.title: Show HN: Neui – Go web apps with a built-in AI agent
candidates.raw_content: Neui is an AI agent and a web framework built as one stack. The core is a server-driven Go web framework ( https://github.com/doors-dev/doors ); neui ( https://github.com/doors-dev/neui ) turns each page into an agent harness. FEATURES: The agent sees & operates UI. Annotate what agent can access (links, inputs, buttons), so agent sees it and can assist user with UI operations or even automate it with scripting. ~>neui.Use{ Desc:"submit the form" } Submit or expose context data for the agent: ~neui.Data{Text: "the product shown in the card", Object: product} ... Dynamic tools, right in the markup Same way as you render a button to the user, you give the agent a tool. No endpoints or lifecycle management needed. ~(if user.IsAdmin() { ~neui.Tool[Refund, Receipt]{ Name: "refund", Desc: "Refund the order", Handler: orders.Refund, } }) Work environment Isolated file workspaces and sandboxed scripting ("code mode") out of the box. Agentic apps When a user needs something your UI doesn't have, agent builds it on demand. Complete chat experience Thread list, history, message edits, full-text search, a message queue and automatic compaction. Batteries included MCP connector, web search and .xlsx tools, rich building blocks library for generative apps. COMPARED TO COPILOT KIT: - Agent thread runs on the server, so browser can't rewrite the history/tools to use your LLM backend + less traffic and faster tool-loops - System prompt and provided tool list do not change during operation - it caches and stays hot (because it's usually the same for all your users!) - Pull-based, targeted UI sync; agent monitors only parts of UI that are relevant to the task (compared to full state attached to any user message) - Neui is already a harness with its own sandbox - just bring your model. - For generative UI agent writes a small app on specialized micro framework; agent doesn't need to answer each click or load user input/API responses into context - CON: Is not stack-agnostic, like AG-UI stuff TRY IT: The repo has a demo app with all of this: git clone https://github.com/doors-dev/neui && cd neui DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=... go run ./examples/business-systems/backoffice Then open http://localhost:8095. Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek and any OpenAI-compatible provider will work. STATUS: Both doors and neui are Apache-2.0. I released the first version about 3 weeks ago, so it's early and I am still optimizing some system instructions. Neui itself took me 3 months, on top of the 2 years I spent on the framework underneath (it's awesome, btw), which made it possible. candidates.title: Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon

Coding gives you a window into what the future will look like for a large amount of knowledge work. The first step for most jobs is that we go from doing most of the research, typing, and value creation manually (even if it’s using digital tools) to soon coordinating the work that agents are doing. Next, as this step itself becomes redundant or slows down what agents are capable of, we will be giving agents goals to optimize against and they’ll go off on and increasingly solve larger problems for us. This may at first blush look like something whose impact gets stuck with coding, but actually a large percentage of knowledge work may eventually just converge with this form factor due to the massive productivity gains that can be generated. Agents will use computers, leverage our existing tools or write new ones, and write code on the fly to solve larger swaths of knowledge work. So even if a task today doesn’t seem to be “coding” directly, the task may eventually fold into being coding adjacent. Manufacturing, architecture, life sciences, material sciences, cyber, and on and on. One big hurdle in the way ultimately will be that much of this work remains non-verifiable, so humans will be even more in the loop than they are in coding. But the part that they can hand off will just get bigger and bigger over time as the models are more capable. So in short, pay attention to coding and you’ll get a sense for where work is going.

candidates.title: I asked Claude to populate a Civilization-style game map with real data from the US. Opus 5.5 downloaded and parse a ton of public data and 7 hours and 45K lines of code later... it works :) - 31 real data sources including Census, BEA, BLS, EIA, NOAA, USGS, DoD, NPS, FAA, FEMA, CDC... - Real elevation, land cover, GDP, jobs, power plants, mines, ports, airports, bases, parks, universities, freight flows, disasters; all reconciled onto one 25 km hex grid. - The data is converted into Civilization language, e.g. Gold yield is GDP. A city's districts are its real industry specializations: San Jose gets a Campus, Detroit is "Motor city". Its citizens are its real workforce: 1 in 4 San Jose workers are engineers, coders or scientists, against 1 in 14 nationally. Wonders are chosen by published rules, such as national parks by visitor numbers and universities by R&D spending, etc etc. - 19 lenses (income, degrees, faith, disasters…), a City View for 524 metros, and nine advisors plus an Explorer. The Explorer turns any column for any of 3,100+ counties into a table and scatter plot, linked to the map. - Claude decided to skip a few states and territories sry - Built using Claude Code desktop app, Opus 5.5 on medium and turning on ultracode. It's deployed here: https://t.co/QMhmafXMj5 and the "?" has the source link too. I don't exactly know where I was going with this but it's really fun to browse and play with. Possibly it can be expanded or built into a game. I only have half of my weekly Claude quote left though so someone else will have to take over :D. Claude also made a trailer:

candidates.title: AI native teams will eventually force the surrounding organization to become AI native too. Take software development. coding velocity is way up thanks to AI, while actual shipped products and business impact are unchanged in most companies. That’s cos the surrounding system of experimentation tooling, evaluation, launch processes, and gtm are outdated. It’s like sticking a Ferrari engine in a sedan and racing it on Indian roads. The engine can rev faster but the car speed is limited by its system and environment. AI native companies were built ground up for this new way of building and shipping. They’re also able to shed suboptimal processes faster. Market forces will quickly force all companies to adapt or perish. If you’re solving this for your company: map out your product lifecycle and rebuild it ground up - tooling, team structure, gtm, everything.
